Issue 4, in force since 3 March 2025.\\n\\n## 1. When this applies\\n\\nA supplier, a customer or our own laboratory tells us that an ingredient lot carries an allergen it does not declare.\\nThe lot is identified by the supplier's name together with the supplier's lot code; the same code from a different\\nsupplier is a different lot.\\n\\n## 2. What is implicated\\n\\n2.1 Every goods receipt of the lot, and every stores tub filled from such a receipt, is implicated.\\n\\n2.2 A tub filled by decanting from an implicated tub is implicated. The stores tubs register records the tub a decant\\ncame from.\\n\\n2.3 A blend or a finished batch is implicated when any implicated tub, blend or batch went into it, in any quantity.\\nWhat went into a run is what its posted scale tickets say. An unposted ticket records nothing until it is posted.\\n\\n2.4 Rework: a finished batch put back into a later batch is an ingredient of that batch like any other.\\n\\n2.5 Carry-over: a run is implicated when the run before it on the same line or in the blend room was implicated,\\nunless the line was validated clean between the two runs. When a line counts as validated clean is set by the\\nclean-down procedure, not by this standard.\\n\\n2.6 Each run implicated under 2.3 to 2.5 implicates further runs in turn, so the trace is complete only when a full\\npass over the records adds nothing.\\n\\n## 3. What a test result means\\n\\nA negative allergen test on a finished batch does not take it out of the trace. Sampling cannot prove a batch free of\\nan allergen that went into it; only the records decide.\\n\\n## 4. Mass balance\\n\\n4.1 For the implicated lot, every kilogram received is accounted as used (posted scale tickets from its tubs, decants\\nexcepted), on hand (the net stores count of its tubs), written off (the write-off register), or unaccounted. Report\\neach of the five figures in kilograms. A decant moves stock between tubs and is neither use nor loss.\\n\\n4.2 Reconcile each tub of the lot on its own: its expected net is what was put into it, less what was decanted out\\nof it into other tubs, less its posted draws, less its write-offs. Its shortfall is the expected net less its net\\nstores count.\\n\\n4.3 A tub whose shortfall is more than 2 kg cannot be accounted for, and is presumed to have gone into every blend made\\nin the blend room between its first and last posted draw whose recipe uses the tub's ingredient. Issue 4, in force since 3 March 2025.\n\n## 1. When this applies\n\nA supplier, a customer or our own laboratory tells us that an ingredient lot carries an allergen it does not declare.\nThe lot is identified by the supplier's name together with the supplier's lot code; the same code from a different\nsupplier is a different lot.\n\n## 2. What is implicated\n\n2.1 Every goods receipt of the lot, and every stores tub filled from such a receipt, is implicated.\n\n2.2 A tub filled by decanting from an implicated tub is implicated. The stores tubs register records the tub a decant\ncame from.\n\n2.3 A blend or a finished batch is implicated when any implicated tub, blend or batch went into it, in any quantity.\nWhat went into a run is what its posted scale tickets say. An unposted ticket records nothing until it is posted.\n\n2.4 Rework: a finished batch put back into a later batch is an ingredient of that batch like any other.\n\n2.5 Carry-over: a run is implicated when the run before it on the same line or in the blend room was implicated,\nunless the line was validated clean between the two runs. When a line counts as validated clean is set by the\nclean-down procedure, not by this standard.\n\n2.6 Each run implicated under 2.3 to 2.5 implicates further runs in turn, so the trace is complete only when a full\npass over the records adds nothing.\n\n## 3. What a test result means\n\nA negative allergen test on a finished batch does not take it out of the trace. Sampling cannot prove a batch free of\nan allergen that went into it; only the records decide.\n\n## 4. Mass balance\n\n4.1 For the implicated lot, every kilogram received is accounted as used (posted scale tickets from its tubs, decants\nexcepted), on hand (the net stores count of its tubs), written off (the write-off register), or unaccounted. Report\neach of the five figures in kilograms. A decant moves stock between tubs and is neither use nor loss.\n\n4.2 Reconcile each tub of the lot on its own: its expected net is what was put into it, less what was decanted out\nof it into other tubs, less its posted draws, less its write-offs. Its shortfall is the expected net less its net\nstores count.\n\n4.3 A tub whose shortfall is more than 2 kg cannot be accounted for, and is presumed to have gone into every blend made\nin the blend room between its first and last posted draw whose recipe uses the tub's ingredient. Each such blend is\nimplicated under 2.3 and implicates further runs in turn.\n"}}},"tool_result_meta":[{"id":"toolu_01Ei1oTkKi4xXx8ogQ6z7KCs","permission_decision":{"decision":"accept","source":"config","reason_type":"mode"}}]}
